LPML.TITLE: V

RB.P: OS: Windows, Linux, macOS, OpenBSD, FreeBSD,\br\NetBSD, Dragonfly BSD, Solaris, other Unix-like

LPML.P: V is a statically-typed, compiled programming language created by Alexander Medvednikov in 2019 inspired by Go, Oberon, Swift, Rust, and other programming languages. It is currently in beta.

V was created due to frustration with existing programming languages being used for personal projects. It was first intended for personal use, but then was publicly shared. On release, the compiler was already written in V. The design goals of V were being easy to learn and use, high readability, increased safety, efficient development, cross-platform support, modern features, and more maintainable software. In 2025, V started being ranked on the TIOBE index, a measure of popularity of languages maintained by TIOBE Software BV.
